title: Day 6 of AI/Algo Trading (Paper) - Posting for accountability
author: Enzobevmax

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
moving the weak longs to a graveyard instead of deleting them is a good habit, you'll want to see later whether they'd have come back.

how many trades did a setup need before it got promoted to Primary?

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
Its a trade count and session count factoring in the confidence metric and break even win rate. So lopsided metrics on a few of those could prompt a promotion. I also like seeing how they behave in different market conditions. Though, I only have 25-ish live sessions of testing under the belt so market conditions affecting these are still not complete stats. 

We do run all through 500 session backtests over 2 years but my confidence still lies with live testing over that. Good questions!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: 25 sessions is thin for regime stuff, yeah, you'd need a few rough weeks in there before trusting it. I'd keep the 500-session backtest as a filter rather than a vote: if a setup only looks good live and dies over 2 years, that tells you something about the live sample too.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body: Yes. Many setups have gone through the back test but have showed a lot of promise in the live testing so its tricky. We now record each live session for mock live replays. Ai says its aboit 98-99% as accurate as live session play outs so even those aren't completely telling.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: an AI's guess at how accurate the replay is isn't a measurement though. the cheap check is to take a few sessions you traded live, replay them, and compare fill by fill. if the replay fills sooner or at better prices than you actually got, that gap is your real number.
